summary:
This Act amends title III of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 241 et seq.) by inserting a new Part W ("Parkinson's and Related Disorders"), adding section 399OO (42 U.S.C. 280n). The primary purpose is to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish and carry out the "National Parkinson's Project" (the Project) to prevent, diagnose, treat, and cure Parkinson's, as defined to include Parkinson's disease and all other neurodegenerative Parkinsonisms (multiple system atrophy, corticobasal degeneration, progressive supranuclear palsy, and Parkinson's-related dementia).

Subsection (c) enumerates the Project's required activities: the Secretary shall create, maintain, and periodically update an integrated national plan; conduct an annual assessment under subsection (d); provide an estimate of current and, if applicable, necessary federal investment; coordinate research and services across federal agencies; encourage development of safe and effective treatments; improve early diagnosis and care coordination; review the impact on health of individuals, caregivers, and families; coordinate with international bodies; and collaborate to prevent duplication of research for related disorders.

Subsection (d) requires the Secretary, not later than 24 months after enactment and annually thereafter, to carry out an assessment of progress on the burden of Parkinson's, including recommendations for priority actions and a description of planned or taken implementation steps.

Subsection (e) establishes and maintains an Advisory Council on Parkinson's Research, Care, and Services to advise the Secretary. Membership includes federal experts from specified agencies (CDC, NIH, FDA, CMS, VA, DOD, EPA, and others) and ten non-federal expert members: two patient advocates, one caregiver, one health care provider, two biomedical researchers, one movement disorder specialist, one dementia specialist, and two nonprofit representatives, with representation of minority and disproportionately affected communities. The Council must meet at least quarterly for the first two years after establishment, convene an annual research meeting with federal and non-federal organizations (first meeting within 24 months of enactment), and provide an annual report to the Secretary and Congress within 18 months of enactment containing a list of federally funded efforts, recommendations for modifying and prioritizing federal programs, and an evaluation of the national plan's implementation. The Advisory Council terminates at the end of calendar year 2035.

Subsection (f) requires federal agencies to share relevant information with the Secretary, consistent with disclosure obligations, to enable completion of the annual report. Subsection (g) provides that the entire section ceases to be effective at the end of calendar year 2035. The Act authorizes the establishment of the Project and Advisory Council but contains no new appropriations.
